title: Foresight AI Brings Gremlin Agents to Reliability Engineering
gist: Gremlin has made Foresight AI generally available as an add-on: four agent roles analyse services, run fault-injection tests, propose fixes and rerun the original test, with human approval required before any test or remediation. The article stresses that evidence so far is vendor-supplied, with no published accuracy or false-positive data, and that the supervised model contrasts with more autonomous agent proposals.

insights.claim: Gremlin's Foresight AI is an agentic add-on to its platform that analyses services for potential failures, recommends changes and reruns tests to confirm a fix works.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Reliability testing vendors are packaging agents as paid add-ons to existing platforms rather than standalone products.
insights.quote: an agentic product that analyses services for potential failures, recommends changes and reruns tests to check that a fix works
insights.locator: Reliability management company Gremlin has announced

insights.claim: Foresight AI splits work across four agent roles: an Analyst that gathers data and recommends tests, a Tester that schedules and runs them, an Operator that interprets failures and proposes remediations, and a Technical Program Manager that tracks coverage and commitments and can send weekly Slack reports.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: The role-per-agent structure mirrors a human SRE team, including a program-management function that targets cross-team accountability.
insights.locator: The product divides work between four agent roles

insights.claim: The main technical distinction is a closed validation loop: after a test exposes a weakness, the service proposes a change and reruns the original test to confirm the fix.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Verifying a fix with the same test that found the problem is the differentiator versus agents that only suggest changes.
insights.quote: The main technical distinction is the closed validation loop.
insights.locator: The main technical distinction is the closed validation loop

insights.claim: Gremlin says Foresight AI will neither run a test nor apply a remediation without approval, keeping an engineer responsible while automating the analysis and repetition around changes.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: The human-in-the-loop gate is the product's trust mechanism and limits how much labour it can fully replace.
insights.quote: Gremlin says Foresight AI will neither run a test nor apply a remediation without approval.
insights.locator: The main technical distinction is the closed validation loop

themes.theme: Proprietary data moat and LLM role

insights.claim: Recommendations rest on Gremlin's Failure Atlas, a proprietary record the company says was built from millions of fault-injection experiments over more than ten years across tens of thousands of distributed systems.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: The defensible asset is a decade of accumulated failure data, not the agent layer, which others can copy.
insights.locator: Foresight AI bases its recommendations on Gremlin's Failure Atlas

insights.claim: Gremlin says customer system data is not used to train a large language model; agents decide using platform data and the Failure Atlas, while the LLM is used only for searching, summarising and explaining results.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Relegating the LLM to a presentation role and promising no training on customer data addresses enterprise data-governance objections.
insights.quote: Gremlin says system data is not used to train a large language model.
insights.locator: Foresight AI bases its recommendations on Gremlin's Failure Atlas

insights.claim: Gremlin's CEO argues that a passing test under realistic load is real evidence of reliability, whereas a quiet alert proves nothing.
insights.speaker: Kolton Andrus
insights.so_what: This positions fault injection against observability-based approaches in budget competition.
insights.quote: An alert going quiet doesn't prove anything. A test that passes under load, in realistic conditions, does.
insights.locator: An alert going quiet doesn't prove anything

insights.claim: Intellyx analyst Jason English describes observability and AI SRE products as useful but largely reactive because they start from telemetry of a problem that has already happened, whereas fault injection creates controlled failures before an incident; Intellyx discloses Gremlin is its customer.
insights.speaker: Jason English
insights.so_what: The argument is commissioned by the vendor, so weigh it as marketing positioning rather than independent analysis.
insights.locator: In a separate article written for Gremlin

insights.claim: Foresight AI generates reports and dashboards from natural-language requests to show changes in reliability scores and addressed risks, targeting the problem that avoided incidents leave no visible evidence the way outages do.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Making prevention visible is a budget-justification feature for reliability teams as much as a technical one.
insights.quote: avoided incidents do not produce the same visible evidence as outages
insights.locator: The service also creates reports and dashboards

insights.claim: Gremlin positions Foresight AI as a response to faster AI-assisted software delivery, with its CEO arguing that more code is reaching production without close human review.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: AI coding output creates downstream demand for automated verification and resilience tooling.
insights.locator: Foresight AI is intended to provide reliability checks

insights.claim: Foresight AI's approval boundary resembles Wix's use of AI in CI/CD, which keeps deployment and critical infrastructure decisions under human control, and differs from Cloudflare's Agent Development Lifecycle proposal in which agents manage more of testing, deployment and maintenance.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: The industry has not settled on how much autonomy ops agents get, so supervised products may be an interim stage.
insights.quote: Gremlin currently takes a supervised approach, using agents to propose tests and changes while requiring people to authorise them.
insights.locator: Those controls resemble the approval boundary

insights.claim: Engineer Sandip Bhattacharya argued that organisations still need specialists to configure agents, assess their behaviour via metrics and adjust them as models and infrastructure change, so automation creates a new system reliability engineers must evaluate.
insights.speaker: Sandip Bhattacharya
insights.so_what: Agents may shift SRE labour toward overseeing agents rather than eliminating it.
insights.locator: In a broader LinkedIn discussion about AI-based SRE automation

insights.claim: Intellyx's English cautions that a reliability programme cannot simply be installed as a software package, since sustained results need shared ownership and accountability across engineering and management.
insights.speaker: Jason English
insights.so_what: Adoption depends on organisational process, which can slow sales cycles and limit pure-software scaling.
insights.locator: English also cautions that a reliability programme

insights.claim: Evidence for Foresight AI comes only from Gremlin and its beta programme; the company has not published comparative accuracy data, false-positive rates or detailed beta results.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Performance claims are unverified, so treat the launch as unproven until customers or third parties publish results.
insights.quote: The company has not published comparative accuracy data, false-positive rates or detailed beta results.
insights.locator: Mike Dauber, a general partner at Amplify Partners

insights.claim: Amplify Partners general partner Mike Dauber described Foresight AI as a trainer who does the reps for you, a comment the author says captures the product's emphasis on repeated testing.
insights.speaker: Mike Dauber
insights.so_what: Investor endorsement is framing, not evidence of efficacy.
insights.quote: a trainer who does the reps for you
insights.locator: Mike Dauber, a general partner at Amplify Partners

insights.claim: Gremlin was founded by engineers with Amazon and Netflix experience; Andrus previously worked on reliability at both, and Foresight AI extends the Chaos Monkey-era approach from running experiments to selecting tests, interpreting results and verifying fixes.
insights.speaker: Matt Saunders
insights.so_what: Founder pedigree underpins credibility but does not substitute for published results.
insights.locator: Gremlin was founded by engineers with experience at Amazon and Netflix
